questions: Are you experiencing involuntary movements of your right arm or hand?
Do these episodes occur while you remain fully conscious and able to respond?
Can you voluntarily stop the movement when you try?
Does the movement occur only when someone touches, moves, or stimulates your arm?
Does it occur when you stand, walk, or change position?
Do you experience sudden weakness or inability to move that arm?
Do you have numbness or loss of sensation in that arm?
Do the episodes begin suddenly and end within a few minutes?
Have you ever lost awareness, stared blankly, or been unable to respond during an episode?
Have you had tongue biting, urinary incontinence, or prolonged confusion afterward?
Have you recently developed severe headache, facial drooping, speech difficulty, or weakness on one side?
Did these symptoms begin after an injury, surgery, stroke, or infection?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Do you have epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, or another neurologic disorder?
Are you taking any medications or substances that were started or changed recently?
results: 1. genetic testing (exome / epilepsy panel): PRNP mutation - familial CJD, which accounts for about 10-15% of cases and is most often E200K

2. brain MRI: restricted diffusion with matching T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right caudate, anterior lentiform nucleus, cingulate gyrus and insula, and less prominently the right frontal, parietal and temporal cortex
3. interictal EEG: generalized periodic discharges recurring every 1-2 seconds as the illness progressed

4. video-polygraphy (EEG with EMG): lateralized periodic discharges over the RIGHT fronto-central-temporal region, TIME-LOCKED with brief EMG bursts under 100 ms in the LEFT wrist flexors and extensors - electrophysiological proof of epilepsia partialis continua
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Familial Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (prion disease caused by a pathogenic PRNP mutation, most consistent with E200K), presenting with epilepsia partialis continua

ALTERNATIVE: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease with epilepsia partialis continua

ALTERNATIVE: Autoimmune encephalitis with focal status epilepticus

ALTERNATIVE: Focal status epilepticus secondary to an acute structural cortical–basal ganglia lesion
dx: Familial Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (prion disease caused by a pathogenic PRNP mutation, most consistent with E200K), presenting with epilepsia partialis continua
